note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment planning following the diagnosis of prostate cancer.

This 56-year-old active dairy farmer is married and lives with his partner. He reports severe lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 20/35, which has been gradually worsening. He exercises by walking 45 minutes daily and consumes approximately 10 units of alcohol per week. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, with no significant comorbidities. He recently attended a biannual dental check-up and a vascular surgery consultation for varicose veins. He has no known drug allergies except for latex.
On digital rectal examination, a palpable nodule is felt, consistent with a clinical T stage of cT2a. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs.
